- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.27–0.53), model shows lag in adjusting to true price direction; add 1–2 days of smoothing or delay in forecast adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage momentum; if sentiment turns bullish late in period, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for final 5–7 days.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
